zh.summary: 看得到資料夾名稱，和能打開裡面的檔案，是兩件事。跟著一個檔案分享案例，學會查資訊、看回應，再說清楚自己確認了什麼。

sourceBody.text: 概念導入
這一課最重要的觀念：發現某個資源存在，不代表你有權限使用它。
例如，你在公司網路中發現一台檔案伺服器，還查到了名為 Finance（財務部）的共用資料夾。這只能證明你取得了某些資源資訊，不能證明你能開啟資料夾、閱讀薪資資料，或修改任何檔案。
這就是 CEH M04「列舉」最需要建立的判斷能力。
想像你是一名受公司委託的資安工程師，要檢查一棟辦公大樓。
從發現目標到確認權限
這是概念上的學習流程，不是所有工具操作都必須遵守的固定順序。某些服務需要先登入，才能進行列舉。
你要區分五個不同問題：

rows: 服務提供哪些具體資訊？

sourceBody.text: 注意： 公司允許你進行資安測試的「測試授權」，與系統授予測試帳號的「存取權限」是兩回事。即使系統允許連線，也不代表你獲准進行測試。
我們先建立三個基本概念。
IP 位址（IP Address）：用來定位網路上的設備，就像大樓地址。
通訊埠（Port）：用來區分設備上的網路服務入口，就像大樓內不同的服務櫃檯。
SMB（Server Message Block）：一種常見的網路檔案共用協定，Windows 常用它來讓其他電腦存取共用資料夾與印表機等資源。現代 SMB 通常使用 TCP 445。
假設你用 Nmap 掃描練習伺服器：
假設得到：

PORT      STATE   SERVICE
445/tcp   open    microsoft-ds
這代表什麼？
445/tcp 是偵測的通訊埠；open 表示從此次掃描位置觀察到該通訊埠接受連線。
但是 SERVICE 欄位的 microsoft-ds 可能只是 Nmap 根據埠號的服務名稱對照，而不是已經完成 SMB 協定驗證。必須進一步確認服務的實際回應。
[Nmap Network Scanning](https://nmap.org/book/man-version-detection.html)
因此：
TCP 445 開放 ≠ 確認有 SMB 服務 ≠ 確認能存取檔案
假設系統已確認提供 SMB 服務，而且公司提供了合法測試帳號 labuser。
你向服務提出查詢：
「這台伺服器有哪些共用資源？」
伺服器可能回應：

Sharename    Type
---------    ----
Public       Disk
Finance      Disk
這一步就是列舉。
我們沒有要求伺服器交出 Finance 裡的檔案，只是要求列出共用資源的名稱。
Windows 提供的 NetShareEnum 函式正是此類查詢的例子。它可取得伺服器上的 SMB 共用資源資訊，而且分成不同資訊層級：例如 Level 0 回傳名稱、Level 1 可包含類型與說明，較高層級的資訊可能要求額外權限。
[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/lmshare/nf-lmshare-netshareenum)
這裡就可以理解一項重要觀念：
資訊揭露程度與操作權限不是同一個維度。
伺服器可能允許某個帳號知道有 Finance，但不允許它閱讀其中的內容。
我們繼續模擬：

texts: 這是模擬結果，代表同一個測試帳號對兩個資源有不同的存取結果。

sourceBody.text: 要解釋原因，先認識兩種 Windows 權限。
第一種：Share Permissions（共用權限）
它控制使用者透過網路共用服務，可以對這個共用資源做哪些操作。
第二種：NTFS Permissions（NTFS 檔案系統權限）
它控制檔案系統中的資料夾與檔案，允許哪些身分讀取、寫入或修改。
經由 SMB 存取 Windows NTFS 檔案時，通常兩種權限都會影響最後結果。不能只看其中一種就下結論。
[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/networking/access-denied-access-smb-file-share)
例如，某帳號具有共用資料夾的讀取權限，但 NTFS 拒絕它讀取某份機密檔案，最終讀取仍可能失敗。
反過來說，即使 NTFS 允許讀取，若共用層級拒絕，透過該 SMB 共用路徑的存取也會被阻擋。
因此，當你看到 Access Denied，你目前只確認了這次操作遭到拒絕。你尚未證明拒絕的確切原因，也不能推論其他使用者一樣無法存取。
以下使用 Windows PowerShell，假設 192.168.56.10 是已經配置好的授權練習主機，且你有適當的測試帳號。
第一步：確認通訊埠
Test-NetConnection 192.168.56.10 -Port 445
如果看到：
TcpTestSucceeded : True
代表這次 TCP 連線測試成功，不代表已經登入檔案伺服器。
[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/nettcpip/test-netconnection)
第二步：列出共用資源
假設取得：

Share name
----------
Public
Finance
這就完成了一次共用資源列舉。指令會依照目前使用的身分及伺服器設定取得結果，因此不一定每次都能列出資源。
第三步：測試指定檔案的讀取權限
Get-Content '\\192.168.56.10\Public\demo.txt'
如果成功顯示檔案內容，就能確認目前使用的身分，在這次測試條件下，可以讀取該檔案。
再測試預先約定的另一個檔案：
Get-Content '\\192.168.56.10\Finance\demo.txt'
如果回覆 Access is denied，記錄這次遭拒即可，不要因此就擅自更換帳號或嘗試繞過權限。
如果你使用 Ubuntu/Linux，也可以利用 Samba 的 smbclient 指令進行共用名稱列舉：
smbclient -L 192.168.56.10 -U labuser
指令會要求輸入該測試帳號的密碼。-L 代表列出伺服器提供的資源，它本身不是讀取檔案內容的操作。
[Samba](https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/smbclient.1.html)
列舉的結果需要放進安全性脈絡中解讀。
假設一個普通員工帳號可以列出整家公司所有部門共用資料夾的名稱，這可能暴露一些組織資訊，但不一定構成嚴重漏洞。
真正應該調查的是：這些名稱是否敏感、業務是否需要揭露、其他未授權使用者是否也能取得，以及系統是否有不必要的檔案存取權限。
從防護角度，可採用三個層次：

items: 網路限制：僅允許需要使用 SMB 的設備與使用者網段連線。
最小權限：對帳號、共用資料夾與實際檔案分別設定必要的權限。
安全稽核：在適當配置的 Windows 系統中，可利用事件 ID 5140 觀察共用存取，利用 5145 觀察共用層級的詳細存取檢查；但 NTFS 層級的拒絕還需要對應的檔案系統稽核，不能只依賴 5145。

sourceBody.text: [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-5145)
最後，資安報告至少要記錄測試時間、來源與目標、使用帳號、查詢指令、實際結果，以及測試限制。
要避免直接寫「Finance 已被攻破」這種沒有證據支持的結論。
現在學的是列舉的共同原理。接下來你會在不同服務看到同樣的概念：

rows: 共用資料夾、部分伺服器資訊
目錄服務中的帳號、群組、物件
設備資訊、介面與管理資料
郵件服務允許查詢的資訊

sourceBody.text: 它們使用不同協定，但問題本質相同：服務會向什麼身分透露哪些資訊？這些資訊是否超過業務需要？

en.summary: Seeing a folder’s name and opening a file inside it are different things. Follow a file-sharing example to learn what to ask, what to look for, and how to describe what you found.

sections.heading: 1. You found Public and Finance. What can you do next?
paragraphs: Start with a made-up practice scenario. You sign in to a file server with a test account named labuser and see two share names: Public and Finance. A server is a computer that provides a service. A share is a file-sharing location you can connect to over the network.

Using SMB—the rules for this kind of network file sharing—you try to download the agreed test.txt file from each share. Public succeeds. Finance returns ACCESS_DENIED: that read request was rejected. The record below keeps those observations separate.

blocks.heading: Start with the result: one account, two file reads
paragraphs: Assume the test is authorized and labuser has signed in successfully. This is a simplified teaching record. In your own lab, save the tool’s actual output.
You can report: “labuser could see the Finance share name, and its attempt to read Finance/test.txt was denied.” Directory listings, other files, and writing each need their own results.

Querying a service for details such as share names, accounts, or groups is called enumeration. Think of getting a department list at reception: entering an office, reading files, and editing them each require permission. Security teams use enumeration to inventory resources and check who can see them.
blocks.code:
445/tcp open
SMB protocol response confirmed
Share names: Public, Finance
\\fileserver\Public\test.txt  → Read successful
\\fileserver\Finance\test.txt → ACCESS_DENIED

sections.heading: 2. Break the result into five steps
paragraphs: Scanning is like checking which reception desk responds. Enumeration is asking that desk for a list. Reconnaissance comes earlier: gathering background such as company names, domains, or system purposes. A tool may do several of these jobs at once; keep their results separate.

Before testing, agree on the host, time, account, and allowed operations. Sign in when the service requires it. Some services allow anonymous queries; record that identity too. The five steps below organize your reasoning, rather than prescribe how every tool works.

blocks.caption: From an open endpoint to a specific file read
blocks.description: Start with permission to test. Record the identity and response at every step, and sign in whenever required.

items.title: Find an endpoint
items.body: TCP 445 is open: the probe observed a program accepting connections.

items.title: Check the protocol
items.body: A response using SMB gives you evidence that the service speaks SMB.

items.title: List share names
items.body: Public and Finance appear: record the names visible to this identity.

items.title: List a directory
items.body: Run ls and record the entries returned for that directory.

items.title: Read a test file
items.body: Run get and record whether the specified file downloads successfully.

blocks.caption: Four foundational terms
rows: An endpoint number, used together with an IP address and transport protocol
A program or capability that does a job
Rules both sides use to exchange messages
A specific item the service manages

blocks.heading: The port is a clue; check the response
paragraphs: TCP is one protocol used to carry data. A result of 445/tcp open tells you that a program accepted connections during this probe. SMB commonly uses TCP 445; inspect the protocol response next.

Nmap probes hosts and services. Its -sV option tries to identify a service and version. Keep the original response alongside the tool’s identification so you can review what supports it. [Port states](https://nmap.org/book/man-port-scanning-basics.html) · [Service detection](https://nmap.org/book/man-version-detection.html)

blocks.heading: Further detail: NetShareEnum information levels
paragraphs: An API is an interface a program uses to request a function from another program. Microsoft’s NetShareEnum is one way to query shares. Its information level selects which fields to request.
Level 0 returns share names. Level 1 adds resource type and a comment. Higher levels request other information, with permissions depending on calling context and platform.

“No special group membership required” for levels 0/1 concerns group membership. Whether an anonymous query succeeds still depends on authentication and service policy. [NetShareEnum documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/lmshare/nf-lmshare-netshareenum)

sections.heading: 3. Separate “Who are you?” from “What may you do?”
paragraphs: Authentication checks who you are, for example when labuser signs in with a password. Authorization decides what that account may do, such as read or edit a file. Permission to conduct a test is the agreement made beforehand; sign-in and access rights are checks the system performs. [Authentication and authorization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/authentication-vs-authorization)
Each card below asks a different question about Finance. They summarize the made-up case and keep the untested actions visible.

Typical Windows SMB access depends on both share permissions and NTFS permissions. Share permissions govern access through the network share. NTFS is a Windows file system; its permissions govern folders and files. If the share allows reading and writing but NTFS allows only reading, access through that path is normally read-only. Also check group membership, rules inherited from parent folders, and allow/deny settings.

When you receive ACCESS_DENIED, record the specific action that was denied. Then check whether sign-in succeeded, review SMB policy and share/NTFS permissions, and use logs to locate the cause. [Troubleshooting steps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/networking/access-denied-access-smb-file-share)

blocks.caption: Finance: four actions, four separate results
blocks.description: A made-up case using labuser. Each card describes one action. Record a new result when the account, path, or conditions change.

items.title: See the name
items.body: labuser · Finance: Observed: Finance appeared in the share list.

items.title: List the directory
items.body: labuser · Finance: To check: record the ls response inside Finance.

items.title: Read a file
items.body: labuser · Finance/test.txt: Observed: reading Finance/test.txt was denied.

items.title: Write a file
items.body: labuser · Finance: To check: obtain permission for this action and test it separately.

blocks.heading: Where should you look when a read fails?
paragraphs: Assuming labuser has signed in successfully, check whether the share permits the read, then whether NTFS permits reading that file. Include any other applicable policies when interpreting the result. This is a troubleshooting guide; the system’s internal check order depends on its implementation.

blocks.heading: Further detail: ABE filters items inside a share
paragraphs: Access-Based Enumeration (ABE) filters the visibility of files and folders inside a share according to access rights. SMB FolderEnumerationMode=AccessBased controls this behavior.

This setting filters items inside Finance. Listing the server’s share names is a separate query. Access controls still decide whether a file operation is allowed. [FolderEnumerationMode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/smbshare/set-smbshare?view=windowsserver2025-ps)

sections.heading: 4. Try it: record a result after each command
paragraphs: Use an Ubuntu/Linux computer with Nmap and smbclient installed. smbclient connects to SMB services. Prepare an authorized server, the labuser test account, and a synthetic Public/test.txt file on the server.

Agree on the host, time, allowed actions, stop conditions, and records you may keep. The address 192.0.2.10 is reserved for examples. Replace it in every command with your authorized lab host. [Documentation addresses](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5737)

Enter the commands in a terminal and enter your password only when prompted. Remove passwords and personal information from saved records. The earlier case was illustrative; record what you actually observe here.

blocks.heading: A. Observe port and service
paragraphs: -p 445 selects TCP 445, and -sV tries to identify the service and version. Find those results in the output and save the original response. An open result establishes a responding endpoint; check the protocol evidence next.

blocks.heading: B. List share names
paragraphs: -L asks for a share list, and -U selects the account. Enter the password at the prompt, then find the share names in the response. If Public and Finance appear, record that labuser’s query returned those two names.

blocks.heading: C. Prepare a download directory in your local terminal
paragraphs: Run this small block in your local terminal. mktemp -d creates a fresh temporary directory. lab_dir stores its path, cd enters it, and pwd prints your current location.

If creation or navigation fails, the block prints STOP. Resolve the error before moving on. On success, it prints the new directory’s path. Check that downloaded-test.txt does not already exist there before downloading.
blocks.code:
if lab_dir=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$lab_dir"; then
  pwd
else
  printf "%s\n" "STOP: prepare the local directory first."
fi

blocks.heading: D. Connect to Public on the same server
paragraphs: After the previous step succeeds, enter this command in the same local terminal and type the password when prompted. A successful connection gives you the smb: prompt. Use the next step’s commands there.

blocks.heading: E. List and read at the smb: prompt
paragraphs: At the smb: prompt, enter one command at a time. ls lists entries in the current server directory. get reads the prepared, authorized test.txt and saves it as downloaded-test.txt in your current local directory. quit closes the connection.

Check each response before continuing. A successful ls establishes a directory listing. A successful get establishes the download of that specific synthetic file. If access is denied, save the message and path, then use the previous section to investigate.

blocks.heading: Record and finish
paragraphs: Save the time, host, account, path, command, and response together. If Finance is also in scope, test its synthetic file in the same way. Confirm permission separately before testing creation, writing, or deletion.
After disconnecting, keep the agreed report and remove your downloaded synthetic file and temporary directory. These steps read server data; cleanup applies to the local copy.

blocks.heading: Tool option: why use interactive mode?
paragraphs: The Samba manual states that -c implies -N (no password prompt). This lesson uses an interactive connection followed by ls, get and quit so that the prompt and each response are clear. [Official smbclient manual](https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/smbclient.1.html)

blocks.caption: Review your notes: what does each result establish?
rows: This probe observed a port accepting connections
The querying identity can see the share name
Denial layer, other files and other operations

sections.heading: 5. Decide whether the information exposure is a risk
paragraphs: Start with the intended audience. Employees may be expected to see department shares. If an outside visitor can also retrieve sensitive department or employee information, investigate who can reach it and why.

Consider five things together: how sensitive the information is, who can query it, who policy allows to see it, which networks can reach it, and how it could be used. Write down the observation first, then explain the evidence behind your risk judgment.

MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base of common adversary behavior. Network share discovery maps to [T1135](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1135/); account discovery maps to [T1087](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/). Legitimate inventory work may use similar queries, so include authorization and context in your assessment.

Use three layers of protection: limit network access, return only the information people need, and set appropriate rights for actions such as reading and editing. Use logs—records of system events—to investigate unusual bursts of queries. After a change, retest with authorized accounts to check that restrictions work and legitimate work still succeeds.

blocks.heading: Further detail: audit scope of 5140 and 5145
paragraphs: Auditing tells the server which events to record. Enable the relevant audit policies before relying on event IDs. Event 5140 provides context for the first share-access attempt in a session, such as the account, source address, and share. To trace individual file reads, also check the evidence recorded at the file-access layer.

Event 5145 (Audit Detailed File Share) records share-object access checks; its failure events concern denial at the share layer. An NTFS denial does not automatically generate a 5145 failure event; examine filesystem auditing and related responses separately.

Preserve time, target, identity, operation and response together. Record a new result when changing identity or network location. [5140 documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-5140) · [5145 documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-5145)

sections.heading: 6. Use the same questions in the next lesson
paragraphs: For any service, ask: “Which service am I querying? What specific information did it return? What can this account do under these conditions?” Use the table as a reference; later lessons introduce each service in turn.

Use the [EC-Council CEH course](https://www.eccouncil.org/train-certify/certified-ethical-hacker-ceh/) and [Exam Blueprint v5.0](https://cert.eccouncil.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/CEH-Exam-Blueprint-v5.pdf) to check enumeration scope. This site’s twelve M04 core topics are an editorial teaching sequence; concept counts vary by module.

The next core topic remains M04-02 DNS enumeration. Accounts, groups, permissions and Active Directory are related further reading, connecting later to LDAP, privilege escalation and lateral movement.

blocks.caption: Common query targets
rows: Mail-service information; recipient verification under specific configurations
Interfaces, endpoints and available remote procedure services

sections.heading: 7. Test: three understanding checks
paragraphs: Choose an answer and think of a reason before opening the explanation. Opening it only shows the teaching answer. Your response and understanding can be discussed separately afterward.

The original small check remains useful as a verbal explanation: after listing Finance but being denied a specific file read, how would you explain the confirmed result and the permissions that still need checking?

zh.question: 什麼是 SMB（Server Message Block）？
answer:
# CEH M04｜什麼是 SMB（Server Message Block）？

一句話解釋：SMB 是一套讓不同電腦透過網路，共用資料夾、讀取檔案及傳送檔案的通訊規則（Protocol，協定）。

你可以把 SMB 想像成「公司的網路共用文件櫃」。

## 一、先從生活中的例子理解 SMB

假設你在一家公司上班，有三位員工：

- 小明：財務部，使用 Windows 電腦。
- 小華：行政部，使用 Windows 電腦。
- 小美：設計部，使用 Mac 電腦。

公司有一台專門存放檔案的電腦，稱為「檔案伺服器（File Server）」。

三位員工可以透過 SMB 與同一台檔案伺服器溝通，但不代表每個人都能讀取所有資料夾。

以前如果小明要把檔案交給小華，可能需要用 USB 隨身碟。

有了 SMB，只要電腦之間的網路連通，而且具有適當權限，小明就可以把檔案放進公司的共用資料夾，小華直接從自己的電腦讀取。

而且兩人不一定需要使用相同的作業系統。

SMB 就是讓這些電腦知道「如何向另一台電腦要求檔案，以及如何傳送檔案」的共同語言。

## 二、SMB 的運作原理是什麼？

假設檔案伺服器的 IP 位址是 `192.168.1.10`。

它提供一個名為 `Public` 的共用資料夾。

你在 Windows 檔案總管的網址列輸入：

```
\\192.168.1.10\Public
```

這段路徑包含三個概念：

| 內容 | 意思 |
| --- | --- |
| `192.168.1.10` | 檔案伺服器的 IP 位址 |
| `Public` | 共用資料夾名稱（Share Name） |
| `\\` | Windows 網路路徑使用的開頭格式 |

當你嘗試開啟資料夾時，通常會發生以下流程：

1. 建立網路連線

   你的電腦嘗試連線到檔案伺服器，現代 SMB 一般使用 TCP 445。
2. 協商通訊方式

   雙方協商可使用的 SMB 版本及相關安全功能。
3. 身分驗證（Authentication）

   伺服器確認你的身分，例如使用 Windows 帳號認證。
4. 檢查存取權限（Authorization）

   伺服器確認你能不能讀取或修改指定的資料夾與檔案。
5. 傳送資料

   權限允許時，你就能開啟、下載、儲存或修改檔案。

以上是簡化流程。實際系統可能重複使用既有登入工作階段，部分環境也允許訪客存取。

SMB 不只是「傳檔工具」。它還支援遠端檔案操作，例如列出目錄、建立檔案、重新命名、鎖定檔案等。

## 三、SMB 和 Samba、NAS 有什麼關係？

這三個名詞很容易搞混。

| 名詞 | 白話文 |
| --- | --- |
| SMB | 網路檔案共用的通訊規則 |
| Samba | 讓 Linux、Unix 等系統提供或使用 SMB 服務的軟體 |
| NAS | 專門提供網路儲存功能的設備，通常支援 SMB 等協定 |

例如，你買了一台 NAS 放在家裡，希望 Windows 筆電、MacBook 都能讀取 NAS 裡面的照片。

這時候 NAS 就可能利用 SMB 提供檔案共用服務。

SMB 是「溝通規則」，NAS 是「儲存設備」，Samba 是「實作這套規則的軟體」。

## 四、為什麼 SMB 對駭客與資安工程師很重要？

在 CEH 課程中，我們關心的不只是 SMB 能不能傳檔，還包括它可能透露什麼資訊。

例如，資安工程師掃描某台伺服器：

```
PORT      STATE
445/tcp   open
```

代表此次偵測到 TCP 445 開放，但還需要確認實際提供的協定服務。

接著透過合法測試帳號向 SMB 服務查詢共用資源，得到：

```
Public
Finance
HR
```

這個動作就叫做 SMB Enumeration（SMB 列舉）。

它只是查出伺服器有哪些共用資源，不代表能夠開啟其中所有檔案。

例如：

Public

允許讀取

Finance

測試讀取遭拒

HR

尚未測試

這三種狀態完全不同。

你必須區分「知道資源存在」、「成功讀取檔案」與「能夠修改檔案」。

SMB 的安全性也很重要。應使用受支援的現代 SMB 版本、設定適當權限，並且避免把 TCP 445 直接暴露在公開網際網路上。舊版 SMBv1 已不建議使用。

## 五、你可以自己試一次

如果你有兩台 Windows 電腦，而且都在同一個允許互相連線的網路，可以做一個簡單練習。

在第一台電腦建立 `Training` 資料夾，利用 Windows 的資料夾內容 → 共用功能，授予指定測試帳號適當的讀取權限。

在第二台電腦的檔案總管輸入：

```
\\第一台電腦的IP\Training
```

如果網路、防火牆、共用設定與帳號權限都正確，你就能看到第一台電腦所分享的檔案。

這是 SMB 最直觀的用途，也是理解 SMB 列舉與權限檢查的起點。

## 六、CEH 理解測驗

問題：

資安工程師利用 SMB 列舉發現 `Finance` 共用資料夾，但是嘗試讀取其中的指定測試檔案時，伺服器回覆 `Access Denied`。

以下哪一個結論最合理？

A. 這代表 Finance 裡面沒有任何檔案。

B. 這代表已經成功取得 Finance 的完整資料。

C. 已確認 Finance 的共用名稱存在，但此次檔案讀取遭到拒絕。

D. 這代表 SMB 服務沒有啟動。

提交答案並查看解析

掌握 SMB 的核心之後，下一步就是學習 SMB 如何查詢共用名稱，以及 Windows 如何判斷使用者的讀取與寫入權限。這會直接連接到 CEH M04 的列舉實作。
explanation: C 對應當次證據：取得 Finance 共用名稱，而指定檔案讀取遭拒。A、B、D 都超出這些觀察。拒絕原因與其他檔案、寫入權限需要各自查核。
editorial: 以下為編輯補充，原始回答保留在上方。所有人物、名稱與回應均為教學情境；練習限已授權設備。本次沒有執行掃描、連線或檔案操作。
Public「允許讀取」描述示例中的測試條件；讀取證據應限於指定身分、路徑與檔案，不能延伸為整個共享都可讀。Windows 經 SMB 存取 NTFS 時要一併核對共享與檔案系統有效權限。

en.question: What is SMB (Server Message Block)?
answer:
# CEH M04 | What is SMB (Server Message Block)?

In one sentence: SMB is a protocol—a set of communication rules—that lets computers share folders, read files, and transfer files over a network.

Think of SMB as your company's shared network filing cabinet.

## 1. Start with an everyday example

Imagine three employees at a company:

- Ming works in finance and uses a Windows computer.
- Hua works in administration and uses a Windows computer.
- Mei works in design and uses a Mac.

The company has a computer dedicated to storing files, called a file server.

All three employees can communicate with the same file server through SMB. That does not mean each person can read every folder.

Before file sharing, Ming might have needed a USB drive to give Hua a file.

With SMB, if the computers can reach each other over the network and the users have the right permissions, Ming can put the file in a shared company folder. Hua can then read it from another computer.

They do not necessarily need to use the same operating system.

SMB is the common language that tells these computers how to request files from another computer and how to transfer them.

## 2. How does SMB work?

Suppose the file server's IP address is `192.168.1.10`.

It provides a share named `Public`.

In the address bar of Windows File Explorer, you enter:

```
\\192.168.1.10\Public
```

The path contains three parts:

| Part | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `192.168.1.10` | The file server's IP address |
| `Public` | The share name |
| `\\` | The prefix used for a Windows network path |

When you try to open the folder, the process usually looks like this:

1. Establish a network connection

   Your computer tries to connect to the file server. Modern SMB commonly uses TCP 445.
2. Negotiate how to communicate

   Both sides negotiate an SMB version and related security capabilities.
3. Authenticate

   The server verifies your identity, for example through Windows account credentials.
4. Check authorization

   The server checks whether you may read or change the specified folders and files.
5. Transfer data

   If your permissions allow it, you can open, download, save, or modify files.

This is a simplified sequence. A real system may reuse an existing authenticated session, and some environments allow guest access.

SMB is more than a file-transfer tool. It also supports remote file operations such as listing directories, creating files, renaming files, and locking files.

## 3. How are SMB, Samba, and NAS related?

These three terms are easy to mix up.

| Term | Plain-language meaning |
| --- | --- |
| SMB | The communication rules for network file sharing |
| Samba | Software that lets Linux, Unix, and other systems provide or use SMB services |
| NAS | A device dedicated to network storage, usually supporting protocols such as SMB |

For example, you buy a NAS for your home and want both a Windows laptop and a MacBook to read the photos stored on it.

The NAS might use SMB to provide file sharing.

SMB is the communication protocol, NAS is the storage device, and Samba is software that implements the protocol.

## 4. Why does SMB matter to hackers and security engineers?

In CEH, we care about more than whether SMB can transfer files. We also examine the information it may disclose.

For example, a security engineer scans a server and sees:

```
PORT      STATE
445/tcp   open
```

This means TCP 445 was observed to be open in that test. The actual protocol service still needs to be confirmed.

Next, an authorized test account queries the SMB service for shares and receives:

```
Public
Finance
HR
```

This is called SMB enumeration.

It identifies the server's shares. It does not establish that every file inside them can be opened.

For example:

Public

Read permitted

Finance

Test read denied

HR

Not tested

These are three different states.

Distinguish knowing that a resource exists, successfully reading a file, and being able to modify a file.

SMB security matters too. Use supported modern SMB versions, configure appropriate permissions, and avoid exposing TCP 445 directly to the public internet. SMBv1 is no longer recommended.

## 5. Try it yourself

If you have two Windows computers on a network where they are allowed to communicate, you can try a simple exercise.

On the first computer, create a `Training` folder. In the folder's Properties → Sharing settings, grant the designated test account appropriate read access.

On the second computer, enter this in File Explorer:

```
\\FIRST-COMPUTER-IP\Training
```

If the network, firewall, share settings, and account permissions are configured correctly, you can see the files shared by the first computer.

This is a straightforward example of SMB and a starting point for understanding share enumeration and permission checks.

## 6. CEH knowledge check

Question:

A security engineer discovers a share named `Finance` through SMB enumeration. When the engineer tries to read the agreed test file inside it, the server returns `Access Denied`.

Which conclusion is best supported?

A. Finance contains no files.

B. All Finance data has been successfully obtained.

C. The Finance share name was found, but this file-read request was denied.

D. The SMB service is not running.

Submit answer and view explanation

After understanding SMB's core purpose, the next step is to learn how it queries share names and how Windows decides whether a user may read or write. This connects directly to CEH M04 enumeration practice.
explanation: C matches the observations: the Finance share name was found, and the specified file-read request was denied. A, B, and D go beyond that evidence. The cause of denial, other files, and write access require their own checks.
editorial: These editorial notes supplement the preserved answer above. People, names, and responses are teaching examples. Practice only on authorized devices. No scan, connection, or file operation was performed here.

Public “Read permitted” describes the example’s test conditions. Record the identity, path, and specific file rather than extending that result to an entire share. Windows SMB access to NTFS files requires checking effective share and file-system permissions.

zh.question: SMB 與 Kafka 是否類似？
zh.originalQuestion: 這是否與 Kafka 的工作原理類似，都是讓電腦之間可以減少互相的直接連線，避免設定與作業系統等等問題，而使用一個協定以及中央伺服器來統一調度與處理文件或資訊呢？
answer:
你的理解方向是對的。SMB 與 Apache Kafka 確實有共同的系統設計思想：透過標準化的通訊方式，讓不同電腦與應用程式能夠交換資訊，而不必直接理解對方的內部實作。

但有一個非常重要的差異：

- SMB 解決的是「不同電腦如何共用及操作檔案」。
- Kafka 解決的是「不同系統如何非同步地傳遞、保存與消費事件資料」。

你提到的「減少系統之間的直接依賴，透過中央服務交換資訊」，其實更接近 Kafka 的核心設計；SMB 雖然也能使用集中式檔案伺服器，但不具備 Kafka 那種完整的訊息解耦機制。

我們從軟體工程與系統架構的角度，來比較這兩種技術。

## 一、用兩張架構圖理解

架構 A：SMB——大家使用同一個檔案櫃

電腦 A 把 Word 文件存進伺服器；電腦 B 透過 SMB 開啟同一份文件。雙方不需要直接交換檔案，但都要能連線到檔案伺服器。

架構 B：Kafka——大家使用同一個事件交換平台

系統 A 發布「收到新訂單」事件；系統 B 負責出貨，系統 C 負責分析。A 不需要直接呼叫 B 和 C，甚至不需要知道它們是否正在運作。

Kafka 的 Broker 會保存事件記錄，Consumer 依照自己的進度讀取。這使得發布者與消費者可以獨立運作。Kafka 也可以由多台 Broker 組成叢集，而不一定是單一中央伺服器。


[Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/intro/)

## 二、兩者真正的差異

| 比較維度 | SMB | Kafka |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 核心目的 | 遠端檔案存取 | 事件串流與系統整合 |
| 傳輸對象 | 檔案、目錄操作等 | Event / Message |
| 架構 | Client–Server | Producer–Broker–Consumer |
| 典型互動 | 發出讀寫請求，等待結果 | 發布與消費可以非同步 |
| 主要解耦 | 檔案儲存位置與使用者電腦 | 資料生產者與消費者 |
| 常見應用 | NAS、共用資料夾 | 訂單事件、日誌、IoT 資料 |

Microsoft 官方文件也將 SMB 定義為網路檔案共用協定，透過 Client 與 Server 互動，而不是通用的訊息佇列。


[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/file-server/file-server-smb-overview)

## 三、更深一層：你其實碰到了「解耦」的概念

軟體工程稱為 Decoupling（解耦），意思是降低系統之間不必要的依賴。

以三個服務 A、B、C 為例：

傳統直接呼叫的設計：

```
A → B
A → C
```

A 必須知道 B、C 的連線位置，以及它們所要求的 API 格式。若使用同步 API，還可能需要等待對方回應。

Kafka 的設計：

```
A → Kafka ← B
          ← C
```

B 和 C 自行向 Kafka 讀取事件。即使 B 暫時停止運作，只要事件仍被保留，B 恢復後就有機會繼續讀取尚未處理的事件。

這種架構叫做 Event-Driven Architecture（事件驅動架構）。

不過，要特別修正你原本想法中的三個細節：

1. 減少的是系統間的直接依賴，不一定是 TCP 連線總數。 SMB Client 要連向 SMB Server；Kafka Producer 與 Consumer 也需要連向 Broker。
2. 標準協定能提高跨平台互通性，卻不能消除所有相容性問題。 仍然需要設定網路、身分驗證、權限、協定版本，以及程式理解的資料格式。
3. Kafka 不等於中央工作調度器。 Kafka 負責事件儲存、傳遞與消費者群組協調；真正執行訂單、產生報表或處理文件的，仍然是應用程式。複雜的跨服務工作流程通常需要額外設計。

## 四、SMB 與 Kafka 甚至可以一起工作

假設你正在設計一個自動處理研究文件的系統。

文件自動分析系統

1. 使用者將 PDF 放進 SMB 共用資料夾

   檔案伺服器負責保存文件。
2. 監控程式發現新文件，發布 Kafka 事件

   例如：`document.uploaded`，包含檔案位置及識別碼。
3. AI 分析服務讀取 Kafka 事件

   透過適當權限從 SMB 讀取 PDF，分析內容並產出摘要。
4. 報告服務收到完成事件

   產生報告並通知使用者。

這裡 SMB 保存的是「文件本身」，Kafka 傳送的是「某件事情發生了」以及相關資訊。尤其是大型檔案，通常更適合放在檔案儲存系統，而不是直接把整份檔案當成 Kafka 訊息。

這種組合在系統工程上很有價值，因為檔案儲存、事件通知、資料處理，原本就是三種不同的責任。

## 五、理解測驗

假設有一家醫院，想讓三個系統合作：

- 系統 A：檢查設備產生一份 200 MB 的影像檔。
- 系統 B：AI 模型負責分析影像。
- 系統 C：病歷系統負責接收分析完成通知。

你會選擇哪種架構？

A. 全部使用 SMB，讓各系統定期檢查資料夾。

B. 全部使用 Kafka，把完整影像檔作為事件傳送。

C. 使用 SMB 等檔案儲存方式保存影像，Kafka 傳遞新影像與分析完成事件。

D. 完全不需要共用儲存或事件平台，讓三個系統直接彼此呼叫。

提交答案並取得解析

最後記住一個系統設計原則：SMB 主要共享的是資源，Kafka 主要共享的是事件。 兩者都能促進系統整合，但解決的問題不同。

如果再往下一層學，最值得一起比較的是 SMB、HTTP REST API、Kafka 三種通訊模型，因為它們分別代表遠端資源存取、同步服務呼叫，以及非同步事件傳遞。這會成為你理解分散式系統（Distributed Systems）的一個重要基礎。
explanation: 本題事件協作情境建議 C：大型影像由檔案儲存保存，事件平台傳遞識別碼、位置及完成通知，分開儲存與協作責任。這是題目條件下的設計建議，不是唯一可行架構；輪詢、直接 API 或其他事件平台也可能符合不同需求，醫院並非都必須使用 Kafka。
A 仍需自行處理輪詢與狀態協調。B 需評估訊息大小、效能與保留成本。D 需設計服務間依賴與失敗處理。實際選型另看可靠性、隱私、既有系統及維運條件。
editorial: 以下為編輯校訂，原始回答與 ASCII 圖保留在上方。原圖 A → Kafka ← B／C 中，B／C 的箭頭表示讀取請求；事件資料回傳方向則是 Broker → Consumer。Broker 可組成叢集，應用程式負責業務處理；圖示不代表單點強制中央工作調度。
原文最後將 HTTP REST API 對應同步服務呼叫，是入門簡化。REST 並不強制同步，HTTP 可搭配非同步工作模式，例如先回覆 202 Accepted，再透過狀態端點查詢處理結果。
保留事件與處理進度仍受保留政策、消費位置及應用程式設計影響；解耦不表示移除網路、資料格式或安全設定。

[Apache Kafka 概念](https://kafka.apache.org/intro/)｜[Kafka Consumer 設計](https://kafka.apache.org/42/design/design/)｜[Microsoft 非同步 Request-Reply 模式](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/asynchronous-request-reply)

本圖的 B、C 各自使用不同 consumer group，才能獨立消費同一主題的事件；同一群組內則分配分割區工作。箭頭表示事件資料流，Consumer 主動向 Broker 讀取。[Kafka Consumer 官方說明](https://kafka.apache.org/41/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/consumer/KafkaConsumer.html)

en.question: Are SMB and Kafka similar?
en.originalQuestion: Is this similar to Kafka: reducing direct computer-to-computer connections and configuration or operating-system issues by using a protocol and a central server to coordinate files or information?
answer:
Your reasoning is on the right track. SMB and Apache Kafka share a system-design idea: standardized communication lets computers and applications exchange information without having to understand each other's internal implementation.

There is one important difference:

- SMB addresses how computers share and operate on files.
- Kafka addresses how systems asynchronously transmit, retain, and consume event data.

Your idea of reducing direct dependencies between systems by exchanging information through a shared service is closer to Kafka's core design. SMB can use a centralized file server, but it does not provide Kafka's full messaging-based decoupling mechanism.

Let's compare them from a software-engineering and system-architecture perspective.

## 1. Understand the two architectures

Architecture A: SMB—everyone uses the same filing cabinet

Computer A saves a Word document on the server. Computer B opens that document through SMB. The computers do not need to exchange the file directly, but both must be able to connect to the file server.

Architecture B: Kafka—everyone uses the same event platform

System A publishes a new-order event. System B handles shipping, and system C performs analysis. A does not need to call B or C directly or even know whether they are currently running.

Kafka brokers retain event records, and consumers read at their own pace. This lets producers and consumers operate independently. Kafka can also run as a cluster of multiple brokers rather than one central server.

[Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/intro/)

## 2. The actual differences

| Dimension | SMB | Kafka |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main purpose | Remote file access | Event streaming and system integration |
| What is transferred | File and directory operations, among others | Events/messages |
| Architecture | Client–Server | Producer–Broker–Consumer |
| Typical interaction | Send a read/write request and wait for its result | Publishing and consumption can be asynchronous |
| Main separation | File storage location from the user's computer | Data producers from consumers |
| Common uses | NAS and shared folders | Order events, logs, and IoT data |

Microsoft also describes SMB as a network file-sharing protocol with client–server interactions, rather than a general-purpose message queue.

[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/storage/file-server/file-server-smb-overview)

## 3. The underlying concept: decoupling

In software engineering, decoupling means reducing unnecessary dependencies between systems.

Consider three services: A, B, and C.

A traditional direct-call design:

```
A → B
A → C
```

A must know how to reach B and C and what API format they expect. With a synchronous API, A may also need to wait for a response.

The Kafka design:

```
A → Kafka ← B
          ← C
```

B and C read events from Kafka themselves. If B temporarily stops, it may resume reading unprocessed events after it recovers, provided those events are still retained.

This is called event-driven architecture.

Three details refine the original idea:

1. It reduces direct dependencies between systems, not necessarily the total number of TCP connections. SMB clients connect to SMB servers; Kafka producers and consumers also connect to brokers.
2. Standard protocols improve interoperability across platforms, but they do not remove every compatibility issue. Networks, authentication, permissions, protocol versions, and application data formats still need configuration.
3. Kafka is not a central job scheduler. It handles event storage, delivery, and consumer-group coordination. Applications still process orders, create reports, or handle documents. Complex workflows across services usually need additional design.

## 4. SMB and Kafka can work together

Suppose you are designing a system that automatically processes research documents.

Automated document-analysis system

1. A user puts a PDF in an SMB share

   The file server stores the document.
2. A monitoring program detects the new document and publishes a Kafka event

   For example, `document.uploaded` contains the file's location and identifier.
3. An AI analysis service reads the Kafka event

   With appropriate permissions, it reads the PDF from SMB, analyzes it, and produces a summary.
4. A reporting service receives a completion event

   It creates the report and notifies the user.

Here, SMB holds the document itself. Kafka carries information that something happened, together with related details. Large files are generally better kept in file storage than placed in full inside Kafka messages.

This combination is useful because file storage, event notification, and data processing are three separate responsibilities.

## 5. Knowledge check

A hospital wants three systems to work together:

- System A: an examination device creates a 200 MB image file.
- System B: an AI model analyzes the image.
- System C: the medical-record system receives an analysis-complete notification.

Which architecture would you choose?

A. Use only SMB and have every system periodically check the folder.

B. Use only Kafka and send the complete image as an event.

C. Store the image in SMB or another file-storage system, and use Kafka for new-image and analysis-complete events.

D. Use neither shared storage nor an event platform; have all three systems call one another directly.

Submit answer and view explanation

Remember this system-design principle: SMB primarily shares resources; Kafka primarily shares events. Both support system integration, but they solve different problems.

A useful next comparison is SMB, HTTP REST APIs, and Kafka: remote resource access, synchronous service calls, and asynchronous event delivery. This provides a foundation for understanding distributed systems.
explanation: C is the suggested answer for this event-coordination scenario: file storage holds the large image while an event platform carries identifiers, locations, and completion notices. It separates storage from coordination. It is not the only workable architecture, and hospitals do not universally need Kafka. Polling, direct APIs, or another event platform may suit different requirements.

A needs its own polling and state coordination. B requires assessing message size, performance, and retention cost. D requires designing dependencies and failure handling. A real choice also depends on reliability, privacy, existing systems, and operations.
editorial: These editorial clarifications supplement the preserved answer and ASCII diagram above. In A → Kafka ← B/C, arrows from B/C represent fetch requests. Returned event data travels from broker to consumer. Brokers can form a cluster; applications perform the business work. The diagram does not imply a mandatory single central job scheduler.

The answer’s final description of HTTP REST APIs as synchronous calls is an introductory simplification. REST does not require synchronous processing. HTTP can support asynchronous workflows, such as returning 202 Accepted and providing a status endpoint.
Recovery depends on event retention, consumer position, and application design. Decoupling does not remove network, data-format, or security configuration.

B and C use different consumer groups to consume the topic independently. Within one group, consumers share partition assignments. Arrows show event data flow; consumers fetch from brokers. en.prompt: smbclient listed Finance successfully, but no file has been opened. What is the most accurate conclusion?
options: Read access to Finance has been obtained
The Finance share name was visible in this query
A high-risk vulnerability in Finance has been confirmed
Administrator access to Finance has been obtained
rationales: A: Reading a specific file is a separate operation requiring an observed result.
B: Correct. The response tells us this account could see the share name.
C: To judge the risk, check the policy, the sensitivity of the information, and how it could be used.
D: Administrative access requires separate evidence.

en.prompt: labuser receives ACCESS_DENIED when reading Finance/test.txt. Which inference is least reasonable?
options: This particular file read did not succeed
Effective permissions and the cause of denial should be checked
labuser certainly cannot perform any operation on Finance
Other users may receive different results
rationales: A: This is what the response tells you.
B: Identity, policy, share/NTFS permissions and logs help locate the denial.
C: Correct choice. A denied read tells you about that read. Other actions need their own checks.
D: Different identities may have different permissions; observe them separately.

en.prompt: Two accounts query the same share on the same server and receive different results. What should be investigated first?
rationales: A: CPU speed is not the priority permission variable in this case.
B: Correct. Compare accounts, groups, authorization policy and other query conditions.
C: Screen resolution has no direct role in server-side authorization.
D: Disk speed normally concerns performance; identity and policy are the first focus here.
